<!-- Answer -->
Native Node.js addons like sherpa-onnx.node often need special handling in Electron builds. Common issues include ABI mismatches (the native module must be rebuilt for Electron’s Node version), missing dependencies, or packaging errors. For Electron 21+, if you see an error like “External buffers are not allowed,” set enableExternalBuffer to false in all sherpa-onnx API calls. If you see an error about unsupported ONNX Runtime versions, check for outdated onnxruntime.dll files on your system.

To help further, could you share the exact runtime error message, your Electron and Node.js versions, and how you’re building/packaging the app? Also, confirm if you’ve used electron-rebuild or node-gyp to rebuild native modules for Electron. This info will help pinpoint the issue and suggest a fix.
